parsed.rationale: Both `WXYCApp.navigateToPreviousTheme` (line 465) and `WXYCApp.navigateToNextTheme` (line 477) live in the same file (`WXYC/iOS/WXYCApp.swift`) and share a Jaccard similarity of 0.75, indicating that roughly three-quarters of their implementation is identical. The only meaningful difference is the direction of navigation (previous vs. next), which is a single parameter. Extracting a private `navigateTheme(by:)` helper eliminates the duplication while keeping the two semantically named public methods intact for readability at call sites.

specifics.proposed_action: Introduce a single private helper method in `WXYCApp` (e.g., `navigateTheme(by offset: Int)` or `navigateTheme(direction: ThemeDirection)`) that encapsulates the shared navigation logic. Replace the bodies of `navigateToPreviousTheme` (line 465) and `navigateToNextTheme` (line 477) in `WXYC/iOS/WXYCApp.swift` with calls to this helper, passing `-1`/`.previous` and `+1`/`.next` respectively. The two public-facing methods can remain as thin wrappers to preserve call-site clarity.
specifics.why_no_category_fits: The two methods are not separate types, protocols, or structs — they are a symmetric pair of near-duplicate instance methods on the same class (`WXYCApp`) in the same file. None of the structural categories (extract-to-common, protocol-inheritance, generic-parameterization, subclass-lift, etc.) cleanly describe the idiomatic Swift fix, which is simply to unify the duplicated body into a shared private helper and keep the two named entry points as one-liners. A Jaccard similarity of 0.75 confirms substantial shared logic worth consolidating, but the right mechanism is a private helper, not any of the named refactor categories.
